question: Episiotomy most commonly used in India:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Mediolateral episiotomy reduces the risk of 3rd/4th-degree tears compared to midline; standard practice in India.
explanations.B: Preferred in the USA but not standard in India due to higher severe-tear risk.
explanations.D: Lateral episiotomy is obsolete; abandoned due to complications.

citation: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e / Gynecology 8e

question: First intervention in hypovolemic shock:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Antibiotics are only for suspected sepsis, not hypovolemia.
explanations.B: Vasopressors are second-line after fluid resuscitation.
explanations.C: Crystalloid bolus 20–30 mL/kg is the first-line action in hypovolemic shock.
explanations.D: Inotropes are for cardiogenic shock, not hypovolemic.

citation: ATLS 10e; Brunner & Suddarth 14e — Emergency and Trauma Nursing
explanation: Crystalloid bolus 20–30 mL/kg is the first-line action in hypovolemic shock.
